_description: $50k Roth conversion with a healthy Taxable account, verifying the new sourcing rule: conversion ordinary tax pulls from Taxable, not Traditional. Single filer, FL, age 60.
_rationale: Single age 60, FL (no state tax), Trad $500k, Roth $0, Taxable $50k. One-time $50k conversion. 2026 single std deduction ~$15,750 → ~$34,250 taxable income → ~$4,000–$5,000 federal tax. Under new sourcing rule: conv ordinary tax (~$4k) pulls from Taxable, not from extra Trad. Expected: withdrawalFromTraditional = exactly 50,000 (conversion principal only), withdrawalFromBrokerage ≈ $4k (the conv tax), rothConversionGross = 50,000 fully executed.
name: Roth Conversion — Tax From Taxable
